'''Aaron Marquez Miles''' (born April 13, 1983) is an American [[basketball]] coach and former player working as an assistant coach for the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]] and had a brief stint in the NBA with the [[Golden State Warriors]]. Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=1}}, he played at the [[point guard]] position. Miles was previously an assistant coach for the [[Florida Gulf Coast Eagles men's basketball|Florida Gulf Coast Eagles]] and a head coach for the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] of the [[NBA G League]]. In 2019, he was hired as a player development coach with the Golden State Warriors.

==High school career==
Miles played for [[Jefferson High School (Portland, Oregon)|Jefferson High School]] in north [[Portland, Oregon]]. The Democrats won the 2000 4A Oregon state championship, beating Tualatin 58–44, and capping a 28–0 season.<ref>[http://www.osaa.org/basketball/records/boyschamps.pdf] OSAA.org Basketball records.</ref> The Democrats finished the year with a No. 4 national ranking and several other players went on to play in college, such as [[Michael Lee (basketball, born 1983)|Michael Lee]] (Kansas), [[Thomas Gardner (basketball)|Thomas Gardner]] (Missouri), and Brandon Brooks (USC).

==College career==
After being named the Oregon 4A High School basketball player of the year as well as McDonald's Morgan Wooten National Player of the Year, Miles attended the [[University of Kansas]], where he starred at the [[point guard]] position for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team]]. He helped lead the Jayhawks to two consecutive [[Final Four]] appearances in 2002 and 2003 and an appearance in the 2003 national championship game. He is the all-time [[assist (basketball)|assists]] leader (with 954 career assists) of both Kansas and the [[Big 12 Conference]]. He was named to the All-Big 12 Team in both 2004 and 2005.

He was also named to the All-Big 12 Defensive Team three times and he finished his college career, in eighth place in NCAA history in assists <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/leaders/ast-player-career.html|title=Assists Career Leaders and Records}}</ref> and in second place all-time in Kansas history in [[Steal (basketball)|steals]].

==Professional career==

===NBA (2005–2006)===
Miles signed in September 2005, as an [[NBA draft|undrafted]] rookie [[free agent]] with the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]]'s [[Golden State Warriors]] for the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]],<ref>[http://www2.ljworld.com/news/2005/sep/30/warriors_officially_announce_miles_signing/ Warriors officially announce Miles signing]</ref> but was released in January 2006, before his contract became guaranteed.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/Warriors_Waive_Guard_Aaron_Miles.html Warriors waive guard Aaron Miles]</ref> He played for the [[Fort Worth Flyers]] in the [[NBA Development League]] for the remainder of that season where he played with his Kansas teammate [[Keith Langford]].

===Europe (2006–2010)===
He signed for the 2006–07 season with the [[LNB Pro A|French League]] club [[Élan Béarnais Pau-Orthez]], a team that played in the [[Euroleague]] that season, and won the French National Cup championship that year. He played with the [[Liga ACB|Spanish ACB]] club [[CB Sevilla|Cajasol Sevilla]] in the 2007–08 season.

In August 2008, Miles joined one of the three [[Euroleague]] teams from the [[A1 Ethniki|Greek League]] for the 2008–09 season, [[Panionios BC|Panionios]].<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/34631/180 Panionios lands assists ace Miles.]</ref> In October 2009, he signed with another Greek team [[Aris BC]] for the 2009–10 season.<ref>[http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/home/transactions/eurocup-2009-10/i/59208/3695/aris-aaron-miles-takes-over-at-point ARIS: Aaron Miles takes over at point] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714164653/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/home/transactions/eurocup-2009-10/i/59208/3695/aris-aaron-miles-takes-over-at-point |date=July 14, 2014 }}</ref>

===Return to America (2010–2011)===
In 2010, Miles joined the try-outs for the Warriors, but was released days before the start of the season.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors_waive_aaron_miles_102010.html Warriors Waive Aaron Miles]</ref> He signed with the [[Reno Bighorns]]. He was sent to the [[Bakersfield Jam]], but was quickly waived due to injury.

===Back to Europe (2011–2015)===
Miles returned to Europe in August 2011, when he signed with [[BC Krasnye Krylya]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/88201/aaron-miles-inks-with-krasnye-krylya-samara.html Aaron Miles inks with Krasnye Krylya Samara]</ref> In 2012 and 2013, he won the [[Russian Basketball Cup|Russian Cup]] with Krasnye, in the second he was named Finals MVP. With the team, he also won the [[2012–13 FIBA EuroChallenge]]. In July 2014, he left Krasnye Krylya.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/126235/aaron-miles-leaves-krasnye-krylya-samara.html Aaron Miles leaves Krasnye Krylya Samara]</ref>

On July 9, 2014, Miles signed a one-year deal with [[PBC Lokomotiv Kuban|Lokomotiv Kuban]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20140712032146/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/138547 Lokomotiv Kuban signs Aaron Miles]</ref>

==Coaching career==

=== College coaching career (2015–2017) ===
Following his career as a player, Miles was hired at the University of Kansas as assistant director of student-athlete development for the 2015–16 season.<ref>[http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article34600500.html Former Jayhawks guard Aaron Miles joins KU basketball coaching staff]</ref> The following year, he accepted a position as assistant coach at [[Florida Gulf Coast University]] under head coach [[Joe Dooley (basketball)|Joe Dooley]], a former coach of Miles at Kansas.<ref>[http://www.fgcuathletics.com/news/2016/7/15/mens-basketball-former-kansas-standout-aaron-miles-named-new-fgcu-mbb-assistant-coach.aspx Former Kansas Standout Aaron Miles Named New @FGCU_MBB Assistant Coach]</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.naplesnews.com/story/sports/college/fgcu/2016/07/15/college-basketball-fgcu-names-former-kansas-star-aaron-miles-new-assistant/87126222/|title=College basketball: FGCU names former Kansas star Aaron Miles as new assistant|access-date=July 18, 2016}}</ref>

=== Santa Cruz Warriors / Golden State Warriors (2017–2021) ===
On August 10, 2017, Miles was named head coach of the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]], the [[NBA G League]] developmental team of the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://santacruz.gleague.nba.com/news/santa-cruz-warriors-name-aaron-miles-head-coach/ |title=Santa Cruz Warriors Name Aaron Miles Head Coach |access-date=August 11, 2017 |archive-date=August 11, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170811060936/http://santacruz.gleague.nba.com/news/santa-cruz-warriors-name-aaron-miles-head-coach/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> After two seasons, he was promoted to staff with Golden State as a player development coach.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/santa-cruz-warriors-name-kris-weems-head-coach/n-5538713 |title=Santa Cruz Warriors Name Kris Weems Head Coach |website=OurSports Central |date=August 15, 2019}}</ref>

=== Boston Celtics (2021–2023) ===
In the summer of 2021, Miles was hired as an assistant coach by the [[Boston Celtics]]<ref>{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=2021 NBA Offseason In Review: Boston Celtics|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/09/2021-nba-offseason-in-review-boston-celtics.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=September 10, 2021|access-date=September 15, 2021}}</ref>

=== New Orleans Pelicans (2023–2026) ===
On June 23, 2023, Miles was hired as an assistant coach by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].
